# 1 Samuel Chapter 7 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 124 | **Source Image:** 1SA_007_page_001.jpg, 1SA_007_page_002.jpg

---

**1** And the men of Kiriath-jearim came and brought up the ark of the LORD, and they brought it into the house of Abinadab on the hill. And they consecrated Eleazar his son to keep the ark of the LORD.

**2** And it came to pass, from the day the ark dwelt in Kiriath-jearim, that the time was long, for it was twenty years; and all the house of Israel lamented after the LORD.

**3** And Samuel spoke to all the house of Israel, saying, "If you are returning to the LORD with all your heart, then put away the foreign gods and the Ashtaroth from your midst, and direct your hearts to the LORD and serve him alone, and he will deliver you from the hand of the Philistines."

**4** So the sons of Israel put away the Baals and the Ashtaroth, and they served the LORD alone.

**5** And Samuel said, "Gather all Israel to Mizpah, and I will pray to the LORD on your behalf."

**6** And they gathered at Mizpah and drew water and poured it out before the LORD. And they fasted on that day and said there, "We have sinned against the LORD." And Samuel judged the sons of Israel at Mizpah.

**7** And when the Philistines heard that the sons of Israel had gathered at Mizpah, the lords of the Philistines went up against Israel. And when the sons of Israel heard, they were afraid of the Philistines.

**8** And the sons of Israel said to Samuel, "Do not be silent from us, from crying out to the LORD our God, that he may save us from the hand of the Philistines."

**9** And Samuel took a nursing lamb and offered it as a whole burnt offering to the LORD. And Samuel cried out to the LORD on behalf of Israel, and the LORD answered him.

**10** And as Samuel was offering up the burnt offering, the Philistines drew near for battle against Israel. But the LORD thundered with a great thunder on that day against the Philistines and threw them into confusion, and they were struck down before Israel.

**11** And the men of Israel went out from Mizpah and pursued the Philistines and struck them down, as far as below Beth-car.

**12** Then Samuel took a stone and set it between Mizpah and Shen, and he called its name Ebenezer, saying, "Thus far the LORD has helped us."

**13** So the Philistines were subdued and did not again come into the territory of Israel. And the hand of the LORD was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel.

**14** And the cities that the Philistines had taken from Israel were restored to Israel, from Ekron to Gath; and Israel delivered their territory from the hand of the Philistines. And there was peace between Israel and the Amorites.

**15** And Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.

**16** And he went from year to year on a circuit to Bethel and Gilgal and Mizpah, and he judged Israel in all these places.

**17** Then he would return to Ramah, for his house was there, and there he judged Israel. And he built there an altar to the LORD.

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

**Verse 2** — Heb. וַיִּנָּהוּ (wayyinnahu): "lamented" — the root נהה carries the sense of lamenting or mourning. The entire house of Israel turned in grieving toward the LORD. Some render this "yearned," but "lamented" better preserves the formal force of the verb.

**Verse 6** — "Drew water and poured it out before the LORD": This ritual act of water-pouring is unique to this passage. It likely symbolizes an act of contrition or total self-emptying before God. The Targum interprets it metaphorically as "pouring out their hearts."

**Verse 8** — Heb. אַל־תַּחֲרֵשׁ מִמֶּנּוּ (ʾal-taḥaresh mimmennû): Lit. "do not be silent from us," i.e., do not cease interceding. The verb חרשׁ means "to be deaf, silent, inactive."

**Verse 9** — "A nursing lamb" (טְלֵה חָלָב, ṭeleh ḥalab): Lit. "a milk-lamb," i.e., a lamb still suckling. This underscores the purity and innocence of the offering.

**Verse 12** — "Ebenezer" (אֶבֶן הָעֵזֶר, ʾeben haʿezer): Lit. "stone of help." Samuel's naming creates a memorial of divine aid, forming a wordplay contrasting the earlier defeat at Ebenezer (1 Sam 4:1).

**Verse 14** — The MT reads "from Ekron to Gath" (מֵעֶקְרוֹן וְעַד־גַּת). These represent the northern and southern boundaries of recovered Philistine-held territory.

— LOGOS (Λόγος)
